messages:
samir: quick heads-up — discovered a nasty SDK vs REST parity gap while trying to integrate batch_embeddings into the onboarding sample. REST supports the /v1/embeddings/batch endpoint and the `model_version` hint, but the Go SDK has no batch API and the python SDK maps `model_version` -> `modelVersion` which the server ignores.

jk: ouch. can you paste repro? which SDK versions?

samir: repro on staging: REST call succeeds and returns embeddings for 10 texts with routing metadata. go SDK v0.7.10 doesn't expose batch and python 0.8.1 sends camelCase and server treats hint as unknown.

samir: curl (works):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-1","model_version":"v2.3","inputs":["a","b","c"]}'
```

samir: go SDK (no batch):
```go
// no ChatEmbeddingsBatch or similar in sdk-go public surface
// folks end up doing client.RequestRaw("/v1/embeddings/batch", rawJson)
```

lena: python SDK snippet (v0.8.1):
```py
await client.embeddings.create(model='embed-1', modelVersion='v2.3', input=[...])
# server ignores modelVersion and chooses default model ver
```

jk: OK two separate issues: A) missing batch endpoint in Go SDK B) param-name drift in Python SDK. Both break onboarding sample which calls batch endpoint and passes model_version hint expecting v2.3.

samir: also noticed auth drift: our OIDC flow issues short-lived bearer tokens with a `scope` claim. the Go SDK auth helper appends `scope=all` as a query param to the token refresh call, but the auth proxy expects it in the request body per spec. staging rejects refreshes causing intermittent 401s in the sample app.

lena: that explains some flaky onboarding failures. is that in SDK auth helper?

jk: yes — the helper was a quick port from an internal library and we forgot to match the newer proxy behavior. will patch.

ops-bot: Note: staging token service will start rejecting query param refresh on 2026-04-05T00:00Z. Coordinate fixes.

samir: additional behavioral drift: SDK retires using a linear backoff for 429s and treats embedding.create as non-idempotent so it doesn't retry; REST docs recommend exponential backoff with jitter and that embeddings.bulk endpoints are idempotent if requestId passed. sample-apps that used SDK got more client failures under load.

lena: so summary: 1) add batch embeddings API to Go SDK 2) fix python param mapping to snake_case for model_version 3) fix auth refresh to send scope in body for Go SDK 4) align retry policy to server docs and expose requestId opt-in in SDK so clients can get idempotent retries.

jk: I've filed a short issue and assigned. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/DEVEX-4350 — title: "Batch embeddings parity + auth/retry drift across SDKs". tagging sdk-go, sdk-py, infra.

devex-bot: Issue DEVEX-4350 created and assigned to @jk. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/DEVEX-4350

jk: plan: quick patches for auth and param serialization this week, add batch endpoint surface to Go SDK (minor API addition), and a contract test matrix that runs a curl vs each SDK (py/ts/go/ruby) comparing outgoing JSON keys and headers. will also add a sample-app ci job that spikes a small load and asserts retry behavior.

samir: short-term workaround for sample-app maintainers: 1) call REST batch embeddings directly via fetch/curl in onboarding scripts 2) include explicit `model_version` in the raw body and set a `request_id` so retries are safe 3) pin to SDK versions that don't change auth behavior.

lena: thanks. I'll add a quick note to the sample-app README and a tiny test harness that uses curl to validate the embeddings step.

jk: PRs incoming: sdk-go PR to add BatchEmbeddings (WIP), sdk-py PR to remap model_version serialization, and an infra ticket to make staging token service back-compat warnings more visible.

ops-bot: CI scheduled: contract-matrix job will run on staging at next SDK CI (approx 2026-04-01 03:00Z).

samir: excellent. leaving this thread here for sample-app maintainers and QA. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
